🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-10-24 23:00 → 2026-10-25 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **Live v1 commitment posted** — A signed commitment binding proof fields and ledger position went live, moving the reveal protocol from design into verifiable running operation. [tg:tawg:5790]

> **zkIE reached end-to-end** — Proof support for two distinct model families landed without manual setup, validating a key step in the agent-wallet integration path. [tg:tawg:5793]

> **Key manifest published** — The signing-key manifest was added to the public repository, making the BIP-340 verification chain auditable by anyone outside the group. [tg:tawg:5800]

## 🤝 **What moved**

### reveal-protocol

_The commitment layer moved from design to live operation, with binding rules confirmed and fixture authorship resolved._

- 繁星之上 (@onthe_stars) **Confirmed** that reveal-time verification must check both the proof identifier and the ledger position against the signed record being revealed, clarifying the correctness constraint on which the whole verification path depends. [tg:tawg:5785]
- Baby Blue Viper **Confirmed** that Pavlo is credited as the author who pins the fixture pack first, that live fixtures represent a replay record rather than a frozen vector, and that repository visibility is aligned — settling the authorship and semantics of the shared test assets so the group can move forward consistently. [tg:tawg:5816]

### zkIE

_End-to-end proof infrastructure crossed a significant integration threshold during the hackathon._

- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Welcomed** Yujie and connected the zkIE hackathon milestone to prior TAWG work in VEC, helping the group understand how the new proof capability extends existing infrastructure and where it fits in the shared Trustless AI stack. [tg:tawg:5794]

### ERC specs

_Reference-code work and deployment evidence advanced both active spec threads._

- javierpmateos **Checked** four reference-code gaps against the current ERC-8183 implementation, moving the gap-resolution work forward in a way that directly supports spec progression toward a more complete reference. [ERC-8183 Magicians](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8183-agentic-commerce/27902/433)
- it44 **Shared** a deployment observation on Ethereum mainnet registries using only public data, providing current registry state as concrete grounding for the ongoing ERC-8004 spec discussion. [ERC-8004 Magicians](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8004-trustless-agents/25098/429)

### onboarding

_New contributors joined the group, broadening the team's combined research reach._

- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Welcomed** Archer, a consensus-algorithm PhD candidate at HKUST who joined during the hackathon, extending the group's coverage into a subfield directly relevant to trustless coordination. [tg:tawg:5803]
- Merlini (@gobross) **Introduced** themselves as Tiago running Vértice Criativo, focused on the recompute side with independently re-verifiable receipts and attestations, adding a complementary attestation perspective to the group's verification work. [tg:tawg:5805]

### infrastructure

_Bot checkpoints confirmed that the contribution tracking layer stayed active across the session._

- The knowledge bot committed a series of layer-success checkpoints through the window, signaling uninterrupted contribution tracking for all session activity. [commit ce163c6](https://github.com/trustless-ai/tawg-daily-contribution/commit/ce163c6ecd7bb4d644889ff452826afcc6c7be51)

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**

- Whether the replay-record versus frozen-vector distinction for live fixtures warrants a formal note in the spec or a dedicated fixture semantics document
- How Archer's consensus-algorithm research background might connect to the trustless agent coordination problem
- Whether the BIP-340 independent verifier work could serve as a reference implementation example in the ERC-8183 or ERC-8004 forum threads

### ✅ **TODOs**

- Close the remaining ERC-8183 reference-code gaps surfaced in the forum thread
- Exercise the live v1 commitment's reveal end-to-end to validate the binding rule in practice
- Confirm repository and visibility settings for the key manifest and fixture pack per the agreed authorship model

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** A correctness rule for the signed record was confirmed in discussion, and the live commitment that the rule applies to appeared in the same window — theory and running evidence finishing each other's sentences before the day was out.
>
> When your spec debate gets answered by live data in the same session, the relay is working exactly as intended. Keep those loops closing! 🚀
